#2101. Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026

When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.

It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.

Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied.

With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional big guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about.

But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way.

Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off.

Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton

McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May.

Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic said of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very important for us.'

Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler said: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team.

'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today showed there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.'

Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table

Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility.

The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork.

At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly.

Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis.

That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed.

Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts.

As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar.

The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time.

Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar.

Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out

As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull showed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards.

Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining.

The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move.

Moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands.

McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves.

'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!'

Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August.

Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team

Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches.

Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so important,' declared Jakirovic.

'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.'

#2100. Manchester United’s tormentor in the Champions League open to move as Bruno Fernandes successor

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United are locked in contract negotiations but they may have already identified his successor at Old Trafford.

Manchester United could have an opportunity to sign Nico Paz in 2027, with the Como midfielder reportedly open to a move to Old Trafford. He is viewed as a a long term replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

The 22-year-old has attracted plenty of attention following an impressive start to the season in Italy. Paz has become one of Como’s most important players, recording six goals and eight assists across all competitions.

His Champions League performances have been particularly impressive, with three goals and five assists in five appearances. One of his standout displays came against Manchester United, when he scored twice in Como’s 4-1 victory over the Premier League side.

According to The Athletic, United are among the clubs interested in the Argentine international, who would be willing to consider a move to Manchester. However, Champions League qualification is expected to play an important role in his decision.

Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with the attacking midfielder.

🚨 Nico Paz currently favours not returning to Real Madrid. #RMFC retain €80m buy-back so Como playmaker could change mind but no sign as yet. Man Utd among suitors should Bruno Fernandes exit + #MUFC appeal to 22yo even if not first choice @TheAthleticFC https://t.co/OYcOgL15rp

United’s interest comes amid uncertainty surrounding Fernandes’ future. The Portuguese captain recently confirmed that contract discussions had been put on hold, despite the club offering him a new deal.

Fernandes is under contract until the end of the 2026-27 season, although United have an option to extend his stay by another 12 months. At 32, the club must also consider their longer-term plans for the attacking midfield position.

Nico Paz fits the profile perfectly to take that responsibility. His performances for Como have been brilliant as he continues to score and provide.

However, United face competition from Real Madrid, who have a buy-back option worth €80 million. Paz is reportedly reluctant to return to the Bernabeu without assurances over regular first-team football, particularly with Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler already ahead of him in that position..

Real Madrid and Como have officially confirmed that the midfielder will remain in Italy for the 2026-27 campaign, with Madrid retaining the option to bring him back for the following season.

There could also be a small advantage for United in their pursuit, with Paz and head coach Mauricio Pochettino sharing the same representatives.

Much will depend on United’s progress during the remainder of the season. Champions League qualification could be decisive in convincing Paz that Old Trafford is the right place for the next stage of his career. Without Champions League football, that might be a tough ask to have him at Old Trafford next season.

#2097. Top 20 most valuable EFL League One strikers right now

Strikers are where the big money lies, and every club across the EFL wants their line-leaders to have high value.

In League One, that's no different, and with the third tier looking the tightest it's been in quite some time this season, a good number nine could end up being the difference between staying up or going down, mid-table or the play-offs, or maybe even going up automatically.

We saw last season how Leyton Orient's third-tier status was heavily preserved by Dom Ballard's goals and how the excellence of Bim Pepple and Lorent Tolaj drove a once hapless Plymouth Argyle side up the division in the second half of the season.

Two of those went for big money to Bristol City this past summer, but which current League One strikers could do the same?

According to Transfermarkt's data, these are the 20 strikers with the most value in the third tier right now.

N.B. All values are initially in Euros - converted to Pounds for the list

MK Dons re-signed Sam Nombe this past summer from Rotherham United for a guaranteed £600,000, which could surpass £1 million if add-ons are met.

The 28-year-old was bought when the Millers were in the Championship off the back of a 15-goal season with Exeter City, and then would score 14 and 12 in the last two seasons at the level in South Yorkshire, albeit last year ending in relegation.

That would have dropped his value, per Tranfsermarkt's ranks, but you'd expect another 10-goal season at least in this free-scoring MK side.

It's been a difficult few years for Gassan Ahadme. His value would have been sky-high after being signed for Charlton Athletic off the back of 11 goals in 29 third tier games for Cambridge United in 2023/24.

But, a couple of dud years, whether that be at the Valley in their promotion campaign, or last season at Stevenage, have lowered that back down, and now he's back at the Abbey, already with more league goals than he's managed in his last two seasons combined.

Bosnian frontman Admir Bristric was an intriguing signing for Leicester City to make this past summer. The 23-year-old scored 15 in 29 in all competitions last season for Slovenian side NK Bravo, and the Foxes paid at least €1.15m (£963k) for his services.

Unfortunately, Emil Riis signed less than a month later, and all of a sudden, Bristric was relegated to cameo roles and was quickly shunned out of League One plans.

His only appearances in the last three months have been in the EFL Trophy and the FA Cup against National League North side Oxford City. Even then, he only played three minutes off the bench against the sixth tier side.

Bristric is taking time getting used to the EFL, but if he remains out of Russell Martin's plans, his value will only decrease.

It's very impressive that Tom Bloxham, at only 23 years old, has 200 EFL appearances, most of which have come in League One. He's been, at worst, a useful squad player for around five years now, at Shrewsbury Town, Morecambe or now at Blackpool.

The towering six-foot-five frontman hasn't properly exploded into a 15-to-20-goal striker just yet in his career, but his duarability and potential contribute to Transfermarkt's value.

Perhaps the new Blackpool boss, once they're in the building, can start to get the best out of him.

Age does, unfortunately, have to play a factor in these values, as if Kyle Wootton was six years younger, he'd easily be worth double. He'd also probably be in the Championship, too.

Instead, the 30-year-old has to settle for being one of the best goalscoring big men in the third tier at Stockport County. He finished second in the Golden Boot ranks last season, but it's arguable that he'd have overtaken Dom Ballard if not for an injury crisis which meant he had to play centre-back for the final month of the campaign.

He's already in double digits this season, and is one of the key reasons why Stockport are so good under Jimmy McNulty, as his aerial threat means that they can go long to him if their patient build-up isn't working. Very valuable to the Hatters, but underrepresented on this list.

A position purely based on potential, Leeds United must be really disappointed that their 18-year-old starlet Harry Gray isn't currently excelling on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, and hasn't yet started a game under new boss Dave Challinor, as of writing.

The England Under-19 international is highly-rated both at Leeds and amongst general footballing circles, with him the latest line of Gray's, who are legendary at Elland Road.

The fact he was loaned out aged just 17 to Rotherham in January, instead of playing more youth football, just shows how developed he already is, and once Gray can finally get clicking at the top end of the pitch, his value will only climb higher.

Welsh international Mark Harris couldn't properly get going at Championship level with Oxford United following his 19-goal campaign in all competitions in 2023/24 to help the Yellows get promoted.

Now he's back in League One, though, his golscoring knack has returned. He's already netted more times than he has in each of his two seasons in the second-tier in the first few months of this term.

Transfermarkt's list shows a green arrow next to his £628k value, too, so it's increased since the start of the season.

Bojan Radulovic's value has definitely increased over the past 12 months or so. His Huddersfield Town career seemed to be over back in January 2025, when he was loaned out to Eredivisie side Fortuna Sittard after playing just 855 minutes of League One action.

He found form back at the Accu Stadium under Lee Grant, though, and netted seven in 15 appearances in the first half of last season. Unfortunately, in 2026, he's had an injury-ravaged year.

Radulovic missed lengthy periods towards the back end of last season, and this year has been in and out of the side under Martin Drury. Nevertheless, he still has a handful of league goals in limited minutes, and a full return would make an already threatening Terriers attack even better.

Someone else whose value has skyrocketed in recent times is Aaron Collins. Plainly put, not many were expecting him to have the year he's currently having based on last season's performances in League Two.

FLW has debated which 15 fanbases generate the best atmospheres and more inside their home stadiums

The 29-year-old was one of the big-money MK Dons captures while they were in League Two, having netted at least 10 in three consecutive third tier seasons, but he only scored six league goals last year.

This season, though, he's scoring a goal a game in all competitions, leading the scoring charts in league action, and was awarded his Wales debut against Portugal in the latest round of Nations League games. Arguably, he could, and should, be even higher.

Jacob Brown was signed by Luton Town back in the summer of 2023 in their first campaign as a Premier League club. He'd netted Championship goals for Stoke City across the previous two seasons.

He's kind of lost his way since, like the Hatters have as a football club, in fairness, and after spending last season on loan up a level in the Championship with Portsmouth, he joined Reading on a free transfer at the end of his contract.

It's been a smart bit of business so far for Reading, with Brown one of, if not the best backup strikers in the division. Almost all of his appearances have been off the bench with Jack Marriott ahead of him, and he's still scored four times in league action as of writing.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Marcus Rashford has not featured since United’s Champions League meeting with Atletico Madrid on October 3. His absence has left Pochettino waiting to work with the forward since taking charge.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has provided an encouraging update on Marcus Rashford, revealing that the forward has started training on the pitch as he works towards a return.

Speaking ahead of United’s upcoming fixture, Pochettino was asked whether he was looking forward to working with Rashford once he returns.

“Yes, I’m looking forward to work with all the players that are injured. Hope that they can recover as soon as possible. I think to have the full squad fit and available to be selected, that is the most important thing for every single coaching staff, no?” he replied.

Pochettino also provided an update on summer signing Carlos Baleba, who picked up an injury during United’s Champions League comeback victory over Roma at the start of November.

The midfielder faces a longer spell out, with the medical staff initially estimating that his recovery could take between 10 and 12 weeks.

“Baleba, the moment was Roma, [when he got] injured, and the medical staff were talking about 10, 12 weeks,” Pochettino explained.

There was more positive news on Rashford, who has now started working on the pitch as he gradually increases his workload.

“Marcus, today I think, started being in the session on the field. I think he is starting to feel much better,” the United boss added.

Rashford’s return would give United another attacking option, as Pochettino still waits for his first win the united colours.

#2095. Manchester United activate Bruno Fernandes contract extension clause until 2028

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have activated the one-year extension clause in Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ensuring their captain remains at Old Trafford until June 2028.

The Portuguese midfielder’s previous agreement was due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, but United have now exercised their option to keep him for another 12 months, according to Sky Sports.

The decision comes after Bruno Fernandes rejected two offers of a new long-term contract, with discussions between the player and the club having stalled in recent weeks.

Bruno Fernandes confirmed earlier this week that Manchester United had offered him fresh terms but insisted that he did not consider the current situation at the club suitable for contract negotiations.

The Portuguese manager wants United to direct their energies on the club’s current situation rather than his contract.

United helped themselves as well with the extension clause. They have now taken away that pressure of Fernandes negotiating a pre-contract deal with overseas clubs which he would have been free to do from January 1. The clause removes that immediate possibility and gives the club some control over his future.

Bruno Fernandes has attracted interest from several clubs in Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Italy but has repeatedly chosen to remain at Manchester United. He has insisted previously that he has unfinished business at Manchester United and wants to win trophies here.

Since arriving from Sporting CP in January 2020, he has become one of the club’s most influential players, scoring 115 goals in 343 appearances across all competitions. He was also appointed captain in 2023. Although his individual accolades have been called out by former winger Ashley Young as selfish, Bruno Fernandes remains United’s biggest attacking threat.

Despite the contract extension, it does not mean a new long-term agreement has been reached. Both Fernandes and United are understood to be comfortable returning to negotiations at a later stage, with their immediate priority being to improve the club’s current position.

#2094. Chris Wilder urged to make 'controversial' Tom Cannon exit decision at Sheffield United

It has been an excellent start to the season for Sheffield United in the Championship.

After a summer of off-field uncertainty that saw the departures of key players such as Andre Brooks, Callum O'Hare and Gus Hamer, it is fair to say Sheffield United supporters went into the season with low expectations, but Chris Wilder's men have certainly surprised many with their strong start.

After scoring a 90th-minute equaliser to salvage a point in a 1-1 draw with Southampton at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night, Sheffield United are ninth in the Championship table, just one point from the play-off places.

As the Blades continue their impressive form, hopes of a potential promotion push will be increasing in S2, but one man who may not be enjoying his current situation is striker Tom Cannon.

Cannon joined United from Leicester City in January 2025 for a reported fee of around £10 million, but he has scored just 11 goals in 73 appearances during what has been a frustrating near two-year spell at the club.

The 23-year-old has netted three times in 16 games this season, but just nine of those appearances have come from the start, and on what was just his second start in the past month against the Saints in midweek, he was replaced by Patrick Bamford at half time.

Cannon was linked with a return to two of his former loan clubs in the summer, Preston North End and Stoke City, but, speaking in September, the striker denied that he was keen to make a move elsewhere.

When asked which player the club should loan out in January, FLW's Sheffield United fan pundit Jimmy, from the YouTube channel Blades Ramble, claimed that Cannon could benefit from a temporary move, either to boost his confidence ahead of a return to Bramall Lane or increase his value before a potential sale.

"It's slightly controversial this one because I'm not sure how many would agree, but I think that Tom Cannon needs a loan away," Jimmy told FLW.

"Some Blades may have given up on him already and would like to get a fee for him because strikers obviously go for a premium, but I don't think his value would be that high at the moment.

"I think there's potential that he goes elsewhere and does well.

"He could be offered out on loan to the Championship, and then, if he does well, it certainly raises his price, but we would also have the option of bringing him back into the fold at United, where he's still got years to run on his contract.

"He could play a part for us or we could sell him on for a higher price than we'd get now.

"I would be looking at potentially getting Tom Cannon some confidence under his belt by sending him out on loan."

Football League World takes a closer look at the best value-for-money signings in the Championship this season

Despite his underwhelming form throughout his time at the club, Wilder has always been publicly supportive of Cannon, and the Sheffield United boss may be reluctant to give up on a player he has devoted plenty of time to developing.

However, almost two years into his spell at Bramall Lane, Cannon is showing no sign of delivering the prolific form the Blades would have been expecting when they paid an eight-figure fee for his services, so Wilder may soon have a big decision to make.

Does Tom Cannon deserve more time at Sheffield United or should the Blades cut their losses? Tell us in the comments below!

Cannon performed better during his loan stints at Preston and Stoke than he has after his permanent moves to Leicester and Sheffield United, so if the South Yorkshire outfit are keen to recoup some of their money, sending him out on loan could be the perfect way to put him in the shop window.

#2093. Manchester United target defender for January window but manager refuses to sell

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have leaked goals this season and Mauricio Pochettino is now set to get some names in January to address that.

United are reportedly considering several options at centre-back, with Calvin Bassey high on their shortlist. The 26-year-old has impressed since joining Fulham from Ajax in July 2023 for €22.5 million and has become an important figure at Craven Cottage. He currently captains Alvaro Arbeloa’s side.

The Nigerian defender has emerged as a potential target for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United look to address their defensive problems ahead of the second half of the season.

However, United have suffered a potential transfer setback after Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa made it clear that Calvin Bassey will not be allowed to leave during the January transfer window.

Alvaro Arbeloa has also confirmed that discussions are already taking place over a new contract.

“I am so happy with Calvin and obviously he is not on sale. No chance that he can leave this club in January. He is happy here, he is one of our captains and one of our leaders,” Arbeloa said about Bassey during his press conference.

Arbeloa believes the interest from other clubs reflects Bassey’s performances over time and is keen to keep him in his squad beyond the current season.

“You can see how he is playing and it’s normal that so many clubs are interested in him. It’s good for him and for us because it means he is performing really well.”

The Fulham manager also confirmed that the club are working on an improved contract for the Nigerian international.

“It’s very important for me as a coach, for the club and we are working on a new contract. I hope he can sign as soon as possible.”

Bassey’s current agreement runs until 2027, although Fulham have the option to extend it for another year. Amid the interest, the club is keen to reach fresh terms before his contract situation becomes a bigger issue.

Pochettino wants to strengthen his options, with the club sitting 19th in the Premier League table after 11 matches. United have a little budget for January and big names aren’t cheap to sign in that budget. Their interest in Bassey is understandable but given Arbeloa’s comment, United need a solid offer to get him in January.

But unless Fulham change their position or contract negotiations break down, United may have to look elsewhere for defensive reinforcements.

#2092. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

There’s talk, behind the scenes, at West Ham regarding the Nuno era that came before and the differences that’ve taken hold under new coach Scott Parker. If anything, on the pitch West Ham have got worse under their former player-turned-head-coach as the slide down the second division continues.

Even with former Hammers legend Mark Noble on the coaching staff, the players look lost and at times without fight or character. Which comes as a shock to supporters who had expected the opposite would be the case with the hugely popular duo at the helm.

As footballers they excelled – but they’re being tested like never before. They still deserve the fans’ support. In my humble opinion. Disagree? Go for it, That’s what we have a ‘comments’ section for.

However, the talk is, apparently, not all doom and gloom.

TalkSPORT’ sAlex Crook, reporting during the Portsmouth v West Ham game, claimed his own exclusive:

“I was speaking to a couple of West Ham staff and they were saying, even if the results aren’t coming, the general atmosphere is a lot better than it was under Nuno.”

If that is the case and there’s progress off the pitch then we as fans will just have to suck it up and get behind this group. They’re the only 26 available until January and whilst they aren’t very good, the majority are at least, trying.

Noble and Parker have to pick the eleven who will try their hearts out and run over hot coals for their manager and their supporters.

At least then the players won’t hang back for fear of being abused amidst away-end ‘ugly scenes‘ after the final whistle as the BBC reported.

#2090. Ange Postecoglou snaps at reporter as he defends Sadio Mane for missing match to be at birth of child - after defeat which saw Cristiano Ronaldo fail to score a penalty

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child

'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most important thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

'(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more important in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

Veltman- unable to add much to West Ham’s offensive capabilities

Footballfancast.com  single out Veltman for special mention:

“The Dutchman, who is averaging 0.5 key passes and 0.1 dribbles per game, was once again ineffective in possession against Portsmouth before being substituted in the 62nd minute.

Veltman has never produced more than three assists in a season in his career and has not assisted more than one league goal in a season since the 2016/17 campaign with Ajax, which shows that he is an even bigger problem [than Piroe] as he does not have relevant experience to suggest that he will turn things around.

Time, then, for anxious glances to the treatment table to see how Walker Peter’s recuperation from his thigh muscle issue is going.

#2088. Chelsea Monitor Jarrod Bowen And Crysencio Summerville

Chelsea’s wide-player search has moved back into focus after the Guardian reported that the club are monitoring West Ham pair Jarrod Bowen and Crysencio Summerville.

The update lands during a busy early market for Xabi Alonso’s incoming rebuild.

The Guardian’s latest transfer round-up states that Chelsea like both West Ham forwards, while an earlier report noted Chelsea and Manchester United had tracked Summerville.

That same earlier update also said Aston Villa, Chelsea and Everton had expressed interest in Bowen.

West Ham pulling away at Stamford Bridge 👀Jarrod Bowen stuns Chelsea early before Crysencio Summerville doubles the lead. pic.twitter.com/Ktwr4pKZGH

Alonso officially begins work on July 1, with Chelsea confirming he has signed a four-year contract to lead the men’s team.

The winger search is not just about adding more attacking names. It is about identifying profiles who can quickly give Chelsea sharper final-third decisions.

Bowen would offer immediate Premier League output, penalty-box timing and a direct threat from the right.

Summerville, meanwhile, fits the younger, explosive one-v-one profile that would sit neatly inside Alonso’s longer-term wing plan.

Read Chelsea has already tracked the separate Summerville angle, but this latest dual link sharpens the picture.

With pre-season closing in, that is exactly the sort of market check Alonso needs before deciding how much of Chelsea’s attacking rebuild should lean on speed, touchline width and more ruthless wide output.

#2087. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

#2086. Moises Caicedo And Kendry Paez Give Chelsea World Cup Signal

Ecuador’s late World Cup surge has given Chelsea a useful development signal through Moises Caicedo and Kendry Paez before Xabi Alonso’s first pre-season friendly on 28 July.

Chelsea confirmed that Caicedo and Paez reached the Round of 32 after Ecuador’s dramatic 2-1 win over Germany.

For Alonso, the contrast between the two Chelsea midfielders matters as much as the result.

Caicedo captained Ecuador through the pressure game, with We Ain’t Got No History highlighting the Chelsea midfielder’s leadership role in a win that rescued their tournament.

Paez, meanwhile, sits in a different phase of his rise.

That should not worry Chelsea. FIFA identified Paez as one of the tournament’s wonderkids, but Chelsea’s bigger win is that he can absorb elite-tournament preparation without carrying a defining role too soon.

Read Chelsea has already looked at how Alonso must handle Paez’s development curve, and this knockout place sharpens that argument.

Alonso inherits a midfield loaded with senior names, transfer noise and immediate pressure.

#2085. Koppen feels the heat as recriminations over one summer signing grow | West Ham News

IT IS open season right now on just about every aspect of West Ham’s play, their squad, their recruitment and their coaching. With the club at something of an all time low in the modern era, mid table in the second division being their lowest standing in living memory, critics are lining up to have a pop at events on and off the pitch.

Head of Recruitment Nils Koppen does not escape.

His marquee signing of Arne Engels has come upper fire from several sources. The Belgian midfielder actually didn’t have too bad a game – by comparison – against Portsmouth, but that hasn’t stopped many from pointing the finger at West Ham’s summer signing,  with Talk SPORT’s Tom Rennie (Reported with glee by the glasgowtimes.co.uk) apparently leading the charge:

I just don’t see one thing Engels does that James Ward-Prowse couldn’t do,” [Rennie said]. “

That £22m could have been spent on RB, CB, LW, GK. Koppen can’t be allowed another transfer window.”

I’d have to beg to differ, Engels’ through ball that set up Piroe against Preston North End was pure Paquetá in his pomp.

Ward Prowse could only move the ball sideways and backwards. In addition I remember one notorious foot race between Ward Prowse and an opposition goal keeper which the ‘keeper won comfortably, leaving JWP for dead over 40 yards.

True enough, Engels may not be the finished article. But he’s more combative in the tackle, faster across the turf and he has been known to pass the ball forwards. A little like Mateus Fernandez, he’ll likely grow into the season and become undroppable by May.

There are plenty in this West Ham side who are not worth their starting spot or their wages but I’d not put Engels even close to the front of that particular list.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Don’t let koppen or parker near the transfer window Get rid now and the coaching staff (seems like a job for the boys) before it’s too late We have not learned from nuno. Needs a complete overall

A much better comparison is Engels with Potts, the equation being Engels = Potts + £15m

Being played out of position doesn’t help Engels game, every week he is being asked to play a different role. That’s a lot to ask of a young player.

Antonio was asked to do the same. He turned out alright for us.

I have never heard of Tom Rennie, but if he thinks the club should sack Koppen after one hastily put together transfer window then I’m not surprised his “genius” has passed me by. How do these people find work?

to compare engels with jwp is ridiculous – jwp was slow pondersome side to side – engels is young has an engine as will get better – his passing will improve and is our future

Nobody is on fire is part of the problem, but Engels is far from the first in line for criticism. Way better than JWP in his time with us, I think memories of just how slow he was must have faded.

Fans and pundits lurching from one scapegoat to another. Hermansen one week, Pablo another , Kilman and now Engels

Engels was not the biggest problem and actually created 6 decent chances the most by far but his fee was excessive and he is being targeted because of that

My old grandad was a Bhoys fan so I’ve watched a lot of their games over the years, when we signed Engels thought it was a great deal, guess what, he pulls on a Hammers shirt and instantly looks half the player he was at Parkhead, what’s happening?

#2084. Martin Ødegaard sends clear message to Arsenal amid Bayern Munich transfer rumours

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Ødegaard has spoken out about the speculation surrounding his future. He has stated he would like to stay at Arsenal for the future.

The captain has also admitted that talks about a new deal have not yet begun. Ødegaard is currently under contract until the summer of 2028. This leaves Arsenal with an important decision to make over the coming months.

Bayern Munich are being linked with an interest in the midfielder according to reports from Germany. The Bundesliga giants are said to be keeping their eyes on the player’s situation.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, Ødegaard was quick to dismiss the speculation. He made it clear he is settled in north London and sees his future being at the Emirates Stadium.

There is no suggestion that the 27-year-old is seeking a move. Although comments do highlight a contract issue that Arsenal will be keen to resolve in the short term.

The Norwegian’s laid-back attitude should be encouraging for supporters.

He has made it clear that he is happy at the club and wants to stay here for the time being. This means that there is no need to panic.

However, Arsenal will have to get him to sign on the dotted line. Leaving his captain in the last year of his contract with no progress would cause an unnecessary distraction.

Since his permanent move from Real Madrid in 2021, Ødegaard has become a key player in Mikel Arteta’s plans. He has grown into a team leader and is one of the most influential players in the dressing room.

His importance has been shown by his inclusion in all 10 of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far this season. He has scored three goals.

This is a big improvement on last season, where he was hampered by injuries and failed to make much of an impact in front of goal.

It wouldn’t be a shock to see Bayern Munich show interest in Ødegaard, but don’t take this as a sign he is close to a move.

There is little reason for Arsenal to consider losing their captain. He brings so much more to the team than just his technical ability and has been relied upon by Arteta to lead by example.

The midfielder was also pivotal in the 1-0 win over Hull City on 7 November, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute to give the league leaders three crucial points.

Arsenal have put themselves in a good position in the title race. Keeping their key players happy will be important in the second half of the campaign.

The Gunners will be focused on their game against Newcastle United on 21st November.

Arsenal fans have no real reason to panic at the moment, with the captain wanting to stay at the club and his comments suggesting he is happy.

However, it would be a good idea for the club to try and ensure his long-term future at the club. Ødegaard is still an important part of Arteta’s strategy, and ensuring he stays at the club would be a smart move.

#2083. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.
