#2041. Arsenal waste chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back to claim Emirates point

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.

Despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break. Although Arsenal were presented with several good scoring opportunities, they continually lacked composure in front of goal.

Despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal. They have maintained their perfect record in Europe, but for just the second time in the league phase at the Emirates, the Gunners have lost points.

Arteta will also be interested to see how much effort his team expended in their pursuit of a winning goal against Manchester City on Sunday.

Arsenal began confidently and quickly forced Dortmund to defend. Noni Madueke was troublesome on the right-hand side, and although Christos Tzolis was presented with a great chance, he failed to score from a cross.

Just ten minutes in, Madueke played a ball into the path of Gyökeres some 25 yards out. The Swedish forward then fired a curling shot over Gregor Kobel into the net.

A stunning goal from Arsenal’s forward was just what they required. Unfortunately, they were then unable to follow up this positive play.

Despite Tzolis’ effort prompting a save from Kobel, Madueke failed to score from the ball’s subsequent deflection. Likewise, Declan Rice was presented with a good opportunity when Martin Ødegaard set him up in a neat fashion.

Despite dominating play in the first half, Arsenal made a number of poor concluding decisions. Piero Hincapié failed to score from a good position, and Gyökeres also shot high from another good play.

Dortmund did not produce much throughout the game. However, Kepa Arrizabalaga did well to save from Joane Gadou in added time.

Arsenal should have gone into half-time with a more comfortable advantage. Instead, they gave the visitors a route back into the contest.

Shortly after play resumed, Beier failed to score despite being presented with a great chance following a low cross into the six-yard area.

Despite Arsenal successfully weathering that period of pressure, Dortmund soon retaliated. Gadou broke through the middle and passed to Beier, who then rounded Gabriel before coolly beating Kepa in the 55th minute.

Arsenal then faced a tougher challenge as they sought to add a second goal against increasingly confident Dortmund.

Arteta brought on Eberechi Eze, and the player quickly became involved. However, his shot was deflected just over the bar.

Continuing to trouble Dortmund, Madueke saw a header from Ødegaard also fly wide. A shot from Guirassy, also deflected, hit the post, and Rice then shot wide on the other side after Eze had provided an assist for him.

Despite having 29 shots at goal, the Gunners failed to make inroads. William Saliba, too, warmed up on the touchline and then did not play. Arteta continued with his existing defensive line.

Whilst Arsenal had much to be commended for in their attacking play, especially in the first half, good chances are of little use if they are not then converted.

Although Arteta will recognise that he should have secured three points, Dortmund have taken a well-earned point away from north London. Now, Arsenal need to swiftly refocus on Sunday’s game against Manchester City.

#2040. Arsenal injury latest: Arteta faces selection headache as crucial fixtures approach

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could not have been in a more difficult position to suffer multiple key player injuries. Mikel Arteta will face a busy period with a Manchester City visit to the Emirates on Sunday and then in December face Tottenham and Real Madrid.

Although David Raya, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are all sidelined due to injury, Arteta has separate issues to deal with for each. However, the timing of their injuries is especially annoying.

The good news is that William Saliba is back in contention. But Arsenal can’t expect a select group of players to magically fix all of their issues. Over the coming weeks the true strength of the squad will be put to the test.

Raya is currently the most affected player. He suffered a shoulder injury while challenging William Osula in the 2-2 draw against Newcastle. As a result, he was also absent for the Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.

Whilst there had been initial concerns over how long Raya would be out for, scans showed that there was no need for him to undergo surgery. Arteta has called the preliminary reports positive. However, he has yet to state if Raya will play against City.

Kepa Arrizabalaga has stepped in for Dortmund, but Arsenal are affected by the absence of their preferred keeper. Raya is reliable and composed and has great passing ability.

These attributes will be of value especially when facing City’s potent attack. Although Kepa has top-level experience, it is by no means a game that Arteta would prefer to be playing with an unstable goalkeeping situation.

Raya may be available again either on November 29 or when facing Brentford on December 2. Much will hinge on the progress of his shoulder in the days ahead.

Arguably, though, Saka’s injury represents a bigger worry. He was sidelined after hurting his quadriceps in a match against Bayern Munich on 21st October.

Arteta has previously suggested that it will take around eight weeks for Saka to make a full recovery. 20th December provides a possible return date, but there are no assurances that he will be fit to play at this time.

We have already analysed how important Saka is to Arsenal – both as a creator and in scoring and providing width. The new right winger will need to be able to create key moments in close games.

As well as losing Saka, Zubimendi is also set to be out for a number of weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem during his Spain duty. He may be available for the December 13 game against Bournemouth.

Without Zubimendi, Arteta will need to make further decisions regarding his midfield. Like Saka, Zubimendi is good at maintaining good structure, and this is key to Arsenal’s game. Finding a suitable replacement will not be an easy task.

There is some good news. Saliba has overcome his back issue and is once again in the squad. In addition, Max Dowman has served his 3-game ban.

Saliba’s return is particularly timely with City’s attacking threat heading to the Emirates. Arsenal need stability at centre-back, especially if Raya is unavailable.

Arteta still has decisions to make. Although there is not a great deal of time, Arsenal do not always find suitable substitutes. The squad is deep enough to still challenge, it will be in these next games that it will become apparent how much Arsenal miss key players.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2038. Arsenal must seize title-race opportunity as Paul Merson questions Manchester City’s chances

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have the chance to put Manchester City’s Premier League title hopes under serious pressure this weekend. And with Pep Guardiola’s side already six points behind, this is an opportunity Mikel Arteta cannot afford to waste.

Paul Merson believes another City defeat could effectively end their title challenge. That might sound dramatic in November, but the gap is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

Arsenal welcome City to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, sitting top with 28 points from 11 matches. Their visitors have collected 22 points and gone four consecutive league games without a win.

The Gunners have been diligently building on this lead and can now add to the misery of one of their main competitors.

But Arsenal must be wary of thinking that Manchester City will continue to find life difficult. In fact, Guardiola’s men often thrive in such situations.

Whilst Merson has not ruled out City’s attacking prowess, two players in Rayan Cherki and Jérémy Doku have the ability to turn games around.

However, it is in City’s defensive phase, where more alarm bells should be ringing. The back-line has appeared susceptible and has consequently been exploitable.

And that is where Arsenal must show steel.

Arteta’s team have only scored seven goals in 11 Premier League games, compared to City’s 14. Much can be said from this stat alone.

Whilst Arsenal have based their title aspirations on great defensive organisation, City have failed to merge their potent attack with the structure that Guardiola requires.

Rather than passively allowing City to attack, the Gunners should exploit the instability in their opposition’s defence. Arsenal are more than capable of capitalising on these openings.

Psychologically, City are well aware that they cannot afford to continue to trail. In addition, if Arsenal dominate the early stages of the game, then City may well become even more desperate.

However, we must not underestimate Guardiola. City have previously turned around games that had gone against them. Arsenal need to ensure this does not happen here.

Merson’s comment that City stands virtually no chance of success following further failure is also quite an assertion.

Arsenal do already appear to have found their feet and can continue to accrue points thanks to their solid defence.

Whilst it would be unwise to totally dismiss City, Guardiola’s side does have sufficient quality to enable them to embark on a successful winning streak. And this cannot be switched off by one result.

As well as having issues to address, Arsenal have also shown problems scoring recently – both in draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund. Against Dortmund, despite having good build-up play, the Gunners were especially frustrated as they failed to score from good opportunities.

And this cannot happen again when they face City.

Whilst this game may not decide the title race, there are still many games left to play, and Arsenal will also go through their own tough periods.

However, the significance of Sunday’s game should not be downplayed. A win would put nine points between the Gunners and City and further entrench Arsenal’s lead at the top.

It will also compel Guardiola’s men to come from behind.

Despite Merson perhaps being willing to dismiss City, Arsenal must ignore such punditry. They must then go on and produce a good game, seize their opportunities and capitalise on their lead.

#2037. West Ham Must Use Souček Or Risk Losing Him

Following the news that Tomáš Souček has the opportunity to leave West Ham for a Premier League club in January, I have to say that I’m becoming extremely worried about the direction of the football club.

Claret & Hugh spoke to one of Souček’s representatives earlier today, and whilst they made it clear that his preference was to help fire West Ham back into the Premier League, it’s clear that he is a man in demand.

One Premier League club in particular is understood to be surprised that Souček has not been playing more frequently for West Ham and, as a result, is happy to test the water to discover whether he’s surplus to requirements at the London Stadium.

In my opinion, this is not something West Ham should consider, not for a moment.

Even before this news, I was going to put forward my case for Souček being involved from the start against Stoke City.

He’s consistently posed a threat off the bench, not least during last night’s defeat at Portsmouth, and has scored three goals as a substitute this season.

In the absence of any sort of goalscoring form from our strikers, Souček would seem like one of the most likely sources of goals in a team which has gone from being free-scoring and among the top goalscorers in the division to one that struggles to do anything other than hit the woodwork.

A lot has been made about West Ham having Premier League players, but I’m not sure how many of them truly are. Souček, however, very firmly falls into that category.

He’s a European trophy winner, an international player, a proven Premier League goalscorer and more than capable of scoring goals in the Championship.

This is a player who signed a new West Ham contract only last month and whose commitment to the football club has never really been in question.

But what has just become abundantly clear is that if we don’t use him, we’re likely to lose him.

And I find it highly unlikely that West Ham will be able to bring in a better player than Tomáš Souček in the January transfer window.

#2036. West Ham Set For Double Blow Ahead Of Stoke City Clash

The London Stadium is a tough venue to fill for West Ham given its huge capacity, even when everything is going well. Therefore, there was always likely to be a reduced attendance against Stoke City on Saturday anyway, given the Hammers’ recent performances and results.

But it looks set to get considerably worse, with many of those using public transport to get to the stadium facing significant disruption.

A number of railway engineering works are scheduled for the weekend of 28-29 November, coinciding with West Ham’s 3pm Championship kick-off against the in-form Potters. Supporters travelling from Essex in particular will need to allow additional time for their journeys.

Essex and Shenfield: National Rail has confirmed disruption to Greater Anglia services, with replacement buses connecting passengers to the Central line at Newbury Park.

Lea Bridge: Engineering works mean Hertford East services normally terminating at Stratford will be diverted to Liverpool Street. There will also be no trains between Meridian Water and Stratford.

There will be no Elizabeth line services through central London due to additional engineering works, although Stratford station itself remains open.

Supporters can also consult West Ham’s official stadium travel guide, which includes information on accessible shuttle buses.

Given the growing frustration amongst West Ham supporters, I wouldn’t be at all surprised if the travel hassle caused by the trains is enough to dissuade the 50/50s from attending the London Stadium. As a result, I’d expect a lot of empty seats on Saturday.

For all those attending, please ensure you check travel before leaving.

#2035. Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he said as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

Wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

The 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

He was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the new manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

None of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a big defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United

The two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

But that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

There was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

But Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

This is how recruitment at big clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has said he wants his players to behave like a big team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

Nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker showed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

He signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

Palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With big money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, currently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history

Of the new managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical issues stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

Lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a new contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

The fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

#2034. Newcastle United identity, recruitment and putting things right

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

In your opinion, what are the key problems that Newcastle United face?

Not the greatest start to the season, so where has it all gone wrong compared to qualifying for the Champions League and winning the Carabao Cup in 2025?

After a poor 2025-26 season and the departures of Bruno Guimarães, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, the club needed to bring in proven replacements.

Instead, Newcastle United have signed young, unproven players. Bazoumana Touré, Aladji Bamba and others are not ready to replace players like Gordon and Tonali. There is also no guarantee that they will ever reach that level.

The summer recruitment simply wasn’t good enough.

Most Newcastle United fans still support Matthias Jaissle but there are concerns about the way the team is playing.

Some have criticised Jaissle’s tactics, he uses the Red Bull philosophy which is built around intense pressing, quick transitions, vertical attacks and athletic players. While this style can be effective, it is not always easy to get right.

Newcastle United need to find a way to make these tactics work with the players they have. In my opinion the performances have not been good enough, questions are starting to be asked.

Another major problem is the lack of experience in the Newcastle United squad, young players need time to develop.

When you are trying to compete in the Premier League you need experienced players in the here and now who can handle pressure and help the team through difficult periods.

Losing experienced players has left a big gap in the squad and Newcastle United need players who can make an immediate impact, not just players who might become good in a few years.

In my opinion, Newcastle United seem to have lost some of the identity that made them successful. The team used to play with energy, intensity and passion, difficult to play against.

Performances have become inconsistent, supporters need to see a team that fights for every ball and gives everything for the badge.

Newcastle United need to get their recruitment right, the club cannot overly rely on young players who are not ready to make an immediate difference.

They also need to find consistency under the manager. The tactics need to suit the players, the team needs to show the same energy and desire that made them successful in the past.

There is still time for Newcastle United to turn things around but changes need to happen soon.

#2032. Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

That was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

“We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

“We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”

The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

Will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

Pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

Surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

Sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

Palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson

That is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

Fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

The Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

He came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

Palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

Possession: Fulham 60%-40% ChelseaShots: 7-13Shots on target: 2-5Corners: 4-3Touches in opposition box: 16-18

An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

The British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from new signings.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

Rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

Chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

Chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

That is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

Moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

Colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

With their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a new deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

Could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.

Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.

We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.

It might be a new season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:

Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

The boos for Fernandez from the Fulham fans got a lot louder when the players stepped on the pitch. Some people chanted something rather nasty beginning with ‘w’ as well.

There were a few boos from the Fulham fans when Enzo Fernandez’s name was read out ahead of kick-off. Clearly the England fans at Craven Cottage haven’t forgotten what happened against Argentina. Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.

“During the week they had a few setbacks. With Moises [Caicedo], and with any [player], we do not want to take too much risk. They were not ready to play tonight. We need to go week-by-week but for tonight they were not ready.”

Chelsea certainly have an army of staff. I just counted 13 staff members helping the players through their warm-up. One of them is the new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, who is carrying around a clipboard, presumably with all his set-piece tricks on it. Culture guru Willi Isa is also out there, as is former interim manager Calum McFarlane.

"The day to day culture that we want to build, they will play an important role" 📈Xabi Alonso explains his choice to join Chelsea and the importance of signings like Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0koZ7ZyYYx

Chelsea’s £117m man Morgan Rogers has just run out for his warm up ahead of his competitive debut for the club. He’s kept in close contact with his best mate Cole Palmer, going through a few passing drills and doing a few keepy-ups. He looks relaxed so far.

"You NEED goals if you want to win games" ⚽️New Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaks about the losses of Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez and the addition of Gonzalo Garcia 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/tbBujmljxm

OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, LoanTrevoh Chalobah ⇢ Como, £30mFilip Jorgensen ⇢ Strasbourg, LoanDastan Satpaev ⇢ Burnley, LoanBenoit Badiashile ⇢ Napoli, Loan

The most interesting piece of Chelsea team news is that there is no Enzo Fernandez in the starting line-up, despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo. Instead, Romeo Lavia will partner Reece James in the centre of midfield, with Caicedo presumably injured. There is still an expectation that Manchester City will bid for Fernandez before the transfer window shuts, but the Argentine is on the substitutes’ bench. As expected, there is no place in the Chelsea squad for Nico Jackson and Liam Delap, both of whom have not travelled and are expected to leave Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa remain favourites to land Jackson, although Atletico Madrid have been showing an interest. Nottingham Forest are leading the race for Delap.

Alvaro Arbeloa hands full debuts to Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, who have both joined from Real Madrid. Shea Charles is on the bench ahead of his potential Fulham debut.

Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix make their full Chelsea debuts this evening. Fellow new signings Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria and Geovany Quenda are on the bench, as is Enzo Fernandez, who has been linked with a move away. Moises Caicedo is not in the matchday squad.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

Off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

Saturday:Hull 2 Manchester United 0Everton 2 Crystal Palace 0Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Brentford 3 Tottenham 0

Sunday:Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0Newcastle 2 Liverpool 2

Let's get it.#CFC | #FULCHE pic.twitter.com/G2M8LknNgV

Monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#2031. West Ham Target January Move For Arsenal Wonderkid

West Ham United are reportedly preparing a January loan move for highly rated Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri as Scott Parker looks to strengthen his squad for the second half of the Championship season.

According to an exclusive from Steve Kay at FootballTransfers, the Hammers have revived their interest in the 19-year-old attacking midfielder, having previously targeted him under Nuno Espírito Santo.

Nwaneri is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund, having joined the German club on a season-long deal in September. However, the youngster has played just 29 minutes across Dortmund’s last seven matches, and Arsenal could consider recalling him before sending him elsewhere.

Having the ability to operate both centrally and on the right wing, Nwaneri could offer Parker some much-needed attacking options.

Ethan Nwaneri has been linked with a move to West Ham

Personally, I would absolutely welcome Nwaneri to West Ham. If nothing else, it could free up Jarrod Bowen to play more centrally.

Clearly, the West Ham captain has lost at least a yard of pace and is struggling stuck out on the right wing. I can’t quite shift from my mind his wonderful second-half performance against Cardiff City, when he was given something of a free role.

Unfortunately, Parker has since reverted to using Bowen as a conventional right winger, and we’re once again struggling to get the best out of our captain.

Whether anything comes of the Nwaneri link remains to be seen, particularly given the complications surrounding his existing loan agreement.

Personally, I think West Ham could do with improving both wings in the January transfer window. And that’s really just the tip of the iceberg for a team that needs serious surgery.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been hit by yet another injury ahead of facing Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team on Sunday in the Premier League.

The Seagulls were in action on Thursday night before lining up against Newcastle United.

The south coast club playing Universitatea Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Fabian Hurzeler needs as many players available as possible as he looks to compete in both Europe and the domestic competitions.

In the 39th minute of last night’s match, the Brighton boss saw Matt O’Riley on the end of a really poor challenge from Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu, who was then sent off after VAR review.

O’Riley tried to carry on but had to be replaced at the break and Fabian Hurzeler admitted after the match that it doesn’t look good for the Denmark international. The Brighton Head Coach revealing that the player’s ankle was very swollen.

This looks set to make it at least seven Brighton players ruled out of the Newcastle United match.

Malik Yalcouye was the latest long-term injury to hit the Seagulls ahead of last night’s game, whilst also ruled out are Kaoru Mitoma (knee), Stefanos Tzimas (thigh), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh).

Making it at least now seven Brighton players set to miss the Newcastle United match, as Joao Costinha is suspended after having been sent off during the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last weekend.

Other than the new injury for Fabian Hurzeler to deal with though, there wasn’t a lot of encouragement for Newcastle United from Brighton having this extra fixture to deal with ahead of Sunday.

The weak Conference League is very different to the demands of the Champions League.

Fabian Hurzeler was able to make eight changes and the Seagulls still cruised to victory against this weak Romanian opposition.

Only Maxim De Cuyper, Pascal Gross and Chema Andres stayed in the team from their Premier League defeat against Hull City and once they took the lead inside three minutes the result was never in doubt.

They were two up after 33 minutes and then when the opposition went down to ten men it was easy street for the Brighton players. The final score ended up 4-0 but if they had really needed a bigger scoreline, who knows what it could have been if they had went all out in this game, rather than having both eyes on Newcastle United less than 72 hours later.

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

I turned on the TV on Thursday night and I was puzzled, why were thousands of Sunderland fans banned from their latest European match?

The Mackems playing at the Stadium of Light in the Europa League.

Only the fifth European home match in the club’s entire history and yet Sunderland fans conspicuous by their absence.

The moment I switched on, the camera was focused on loads of sections of the Stadium of Light that were totally empty, no Sunderland fans in them at all.

I thought maybe I hadn’t heard of some UEFA ban that had forced them to close large parts of their stadium.

However, when the camera then focused elsewhere, there were many many empty seats in the areas of the ground that were open.

The match was woeful, the quality shocking, the only excitement when the cameras went back to the stands.

It turns out the embarrassing number of empty seats would have been far worse but for loads of Jagiellonia Bialystok fans buying tickets amongst the Sunderland fans. Turns out the Polish team had seen their supporters banned from attending this match due to past misbehaviour.

This type of thing rarely ends well when you have a set of away fans banned and a home club that struggles to sell their tickets. Sure enough, the Police seemed to be having to wade into any number of sections to deal with friction between the Sunderland fans and the visiting supporters amongst them.

If you thought things couldn’t get any worse for West Ham, they certainly did last night, with the club dropping down to 13th in the EFL Championship. Four games took place on Wednesday evening, and the results made pretty grim reading for Hammers fans.

Blackburn Rovers leapfrogged West Ham courtesy of a 1-0 win away at Watford, with Todd Cantwell scoring from the penalty spot. Meanwhile, Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley, and West Bromwich Albion secured a 3-1 victory away at Bolton Wanderers.

Perhaps most worryingly of all, given West Ham’s next opponents, Stoke City recorded their fifth successive Championship victory by beating Millwall 2-1. As reported by the EFL’s official website, George Hirst scored both goals for the Potters.

The Hammers are already 11 points adrift of the automatic promotion places and eight behind West Brom.

With rampant Stoke City next up for Scott Parker’s team at the London Stadium on Saturday, things aren’t getting any easier. We’re going to have to start winning games just to prevent what is already becoming quite a sizeable gap from getting any bigger.

#2027. Nick Woltemade agent quizzed on transfer claim ‘These reports are completely untrue’

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Nick Woltemade continues to make headlines.

The German international striker had a rollercoaster first season at Newcastle United, starting off in great form and then a bit like the team overall, found things more difficult as the 2025-26 campaign progressed and a 58 game season was far too much for a small squad to deal with.

A lot of nonsense written and spoken about Nick Woltemade with ridiculous claims he had been a total flop, despite having 14 direct goal involvements including scoring 11.

The decision was made for Nick Woltemade to spend the 2026-27 season with Juventus, Matthias Jaissle wanting to have pace as his main focus up front.

The hope being that a year of regular football in Italy will help Nick Woltemade improve his skill set, become better at holding the ball up, polish his goalscoring technique and so on. Helping him then to come back and be a bigger asset for the Newcastle United team, or command a significant transfer fee boosted by his time with Juventus.

Big Nick has had mixed fortunes with Juventus, not getting the amount of game time he would like (seven starts in all competitions, eight sub appearances) but doing very decently in the time he has spent on the pitch (five goals and three assists so far).

Last weekend with Juventus drawing 0-0 at home and booed off at half-time, Nick Woltemade was introduced for the second half and within 14 minutes had turned the game around, scoring one and then getting an assist. Juventus finally winning 4-0 at the end against Venezia and the United loan star picking up the MOTM award.

It was bench duties again last night, Nick Woltemade coming on in the second half with Juventus leading 3-1 against Omonia Nicosia in the second half and the Newcastle United loan striker helping his side to an eventual 4-1 victory.

A lot of daft transfer claims floating about and now the United striker’s agent has shot down one of the daftest.

Al-Maidan contacted Danny Bachmann, Nick Woltemade’s agent, to ask about media claims of Newcastle United doing a January 2027 swap deal, with 30-year-old Ivan Toney (reported to be on £20million a year/£400k a week, plus Toney has a court date to face in London after having been arrested and charged with an alleged serious assault in a nightclub) to come to United from Al Ahli and 24-year-old Nick Woltemade to join the Saudi club.

Danny Bachmann dismissing this speculation as laughable nonsense: “These reports are completely untrue.”

The player’s agent making clear what the obvious reality is: “The player’s future will be decided at the end of the season when he returns to Newcastle United. We don’t know yet whether he will stay or leave.”

#2026. Parker Drops Hint Over West Ham Goalkeeping Change

West Ham head coach Scott Parker has refused to commit to either Mads Hermansen or Fin Herrick ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash against Stoke City. The Hammers boss was asked about his goalkeeping selection during today’s pre-match press conference and was decidedly non-committal.

Speaking to the club’s official website, Parker said: “I’ve been hugely impressed with both Mads [Hermansen] and Fin [Herrick], so we’ll manage things, keep working hard and then make our decision.”

“As always, we’ll see. The goalkeeping position is probably one of the hardest on the pitch. You’re there for all eyes to see.”

Personally, I would start with Mads Hermansen in goal against Stoke City. I completely understand why Scott Parker chose to go with Fin Herrick over the last couple of games, but the truth is it hasn’t worked.

I’ve little doubt that the last couple of performances will have dented the young keeper’s confidence, and taking him out of the firing line might not be a bad thing.

Hermansen, whose recent performances have seen him dropped from the West Ham team

Unfortunately, we’re currently in a situation where it’s a case of picking whoever is the least worst, rather than selecting a player because they’ve done something impressive.

If Parker’s non-committal comments are anything to go by, I suspect we’ll see Hermansen reinstated to the team to face Stoke.

#2025. Chelsea star Emmanuel Emegha ROBBED by phone snatcher in London after leaving Stamford Bridge following 4-1 hammering by Leeds

Published: 18:28 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:19 EST, 23 November 2026

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.

Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.

Daily Mail Sport approached Chelsea and the Metropolitan Police on Sunday morning after hearing that the forward's mobile phone had been stolen after he left the stadium the night before.

Neither stood up the information, but Emegha has now confirmed there was an incident, writing in an Instagram post on Sunday night: 'Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.'

Emegha signed for Chelsea from Strasbourg in the summer on a pre-agreement. The transfer fee between the sister sides has never been disclosed. He has won two caps for the Netherlands national team to date.

An interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he said: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds

On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club

'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'

It coincided with him being handed his first start for the Blues and scoring his first goal via a nice left-footed finish. However, Chelsea's 1-0 lead lasted only three minutes as Leeds capitalised on suspect defending to equalise, and then deservedly won.

Noah Okafor scored twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson got one goal each.
