#2023. West Ham v Stoke Preview: Predicted Lineups As Pressure Mounts On Parker

West Ham United v Stoke City EFL Championship, London Stadium, Saturday 28 November 2026, 3pm GMT

Scott Parker is under massive pressure at West Ham. In most circumstances, no head coach should face any sort of scrutiny after four games, but managing the Hammers is a very nuanced challenge and he will not be given an infinite amount of time to turn this around.

For a club possessing arguably the most expensive squad in the division, and one which broke the Championship transfer record to sign Arne Engels, spiralling down the league is not acceptable. Parker has inherited plenty of problems, but he was also appointed to deliver immediate promotion.

A rousing 3-3 comeback at Cardiff City has been followed by defeats against Blackburn Rovers and Portsmouth, either side of a disappointing home draw with bottom club Preston North End. Parker is still searching for his first victory, while second-placed Stoke arrive at London Stadium on a five-match winning run.

Having watched Tuesday night’s game from the second row at Fratton Park, I was frightened by the lack of belief in some of our players. The 1-0 defeat against Portsmouth was not just another unlucky result in which West Ham failed to convert chances.

The team looked fragile, uncertain and short of attacking inspiration. Portsmouth were able to handle us comfortably, and West Ham have now collected only two points from the last 18 available.

Parker is already under huge pressure at West Ham

Parker said after the game that the group needs to “fix up” and give itself a platform, while acknowledging the need to rebuild the players’ belief. That was perhaps the most worrying aspect of the defeat because this is a squad which should not require a confidence transplant before every Championship fixture.

Parker’s immediate job is to get West Ham to the January transfer window without becoming completely cut adrift. There is still enough time to rescue the season, but the Hammers cannot continue losing ground while waiting for injured players to return or new signings to arrive.

I would take this opportunity to make numerous changes. Parker is nowhere near discovering his first-choice XI, so there is probably little harm in experimenting because there is currently very little for him to build upon.

Both full-back positions need addressing, as do West Ham’s striking problems. If I were selecting the team, I would consider playing Arne Engels at right-back simply to try something different, with Ollie Scarles coming in on the opposite side.

However, I don’t expect Parker to make too many changes. The Hammers head coach continues to speak about consistency and stability, so he is unlikely to rip everything up after only four matches.

Joël Veltman struggled badly at Fratton Park, but Parker has very few alternatives while Kyle Walker-Peters remains injured. As Claret & Hugh highlighted following the Portsmouth defeat, Engels may be the only realistic emergency option unless Parker turns to an academy player.

I suspect Veltman will keep his place, with Ezra Mayers continuing at left-back. Maximilian Kilman and Konstantinos Mavropanos should remain together in central defence.

If Parker has any sense at all, he will draft Tomáš Souček back into the starting line-up. West Ham require leadership, physicality and somebody capable of attacking the penalty area, particularly while the recognised strikers continue to struggle.

I also expect Parker to continue using a defensive midfielder. The only question is whether Edson Álvarez has recovered sufficiently to start again after an extremely intense week.

Álvarez had barely played serious football for months before returning against Preston and then starting at Portsmouth three days later. It would not surprise me if Parker rested him against Stoke before getting the Mexican ready to play regularly throughout the busy Christmas period.

Nevertheless, my best guess is that Álvarez will start behind Engels and Souček. Parker needs a result, and this does not feel like an obvious occasion to remove one of the few players who has improved the midfield.

Jarrod Bowen should continue on the right, although I would still prefer to see West Ham’s best attacking player used more centrally. Edvin Austbø is likely to retain his position on the left, with Joël Piroe starting up front largely because Parker has so few convincing alternatives.

Stoke arrive at London Stadium as the Championship’s form team, sitting second after five consecutive victories and an unbeaten run stretching to seven matches. Wednesday night’s 2-1 win over Millwall continued a sequence in which the Potters have lost only once in their last 14 league outings, so this is about as difficult as it gets for a West Ham side without a win in six.

Former Hammers Ben Johnson and Aaron Cresswell could both feature, with Cresswell making his first appearance of the season as a late substitute against Millwall. Djibril Soumaré and Lamine Cissé are fitness doubts, while Luca Bombino is available again after completing his one-match suspension.

Stoke travel to London Stadium as the most in-form team in the Championship, having won five consecutive matches and gone unbeaten in seven. They have lost just once in their last 14 league outings and currently sit second in the table.

Former Hammer Ben Johnson will also arrive with a point to prove, while Aaron Cresswell could feature after making his first appearance of the season during Wednesday’s 2-1 victory over Millwall. West Ham’s official team news confirms that Walker-Peters and Alphonse Areola are still being assessed.

Considering West Ham could not beat the division’s bottom club and were then comfortably handled by Portsmouth, I’m struggling to find any convincing reason to predict victory against the Championship’s best-performing side.

I hope I’m wrong, but nothing I have seen from Parker’s West Ham suggests we are ready to beat Stoke.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

We need grafters in this team. Get Souchek in the team he’s a fighter. One of our best midfields was Rice and Souchek with Rice holding and Souchek getting forward with late runs into the box. We need grafters. Souchek, Alvarez, Bowen, Mavrapanos all solid grafters, just need seven more.

It’s this entitled attitude that has got us where we are. From everyone, players and fans alike. It’s not a given that we should be top of this league. This team is weaker than the one that got relegated. We’ve got players who are either too young or too old: not ready yet, or past their best. We’ve also got a fan base with no patience. We boo players even when they’ve played well and bad luck has cost them a result. And there are always fans who want the manager out after no time at all, no matter who he is. Perhaps we need another year in the Championship to eat a bit more humble pie

I think you have a few in there that should never wear the shirt again. My XI Areola (he should be at 90% by now) Veltman Mav Golumbakis Boiro (let’s see what he can do) Ajala Alvarez Mukasa Magassa Austbø Bowen

I can see no reason to predict a win either, we’re at a low ebb while Stoke are on top form, anyone dispassionate looking at it wouldn’t predict us to win.

Perhaps we can raise our game or Stoke will have an off day, who knows, although that doesn’t seem likely all manner of things can happen in football.

We look a million miles off promotion candidates but I’ll be as hopeful as ever on Saturday at 3pm

#2021. “Pablo Price Drop” West Ham Stunned By Striker’s Dramatic Drop In Value

The true extent of West Ham striker Pablo Felipe’s depreciation in value has been laid bare following a transfer offer from a Portuguese club. The Brazilian striker moved to the London Stadium from Gil Vicente for over €20 million less than a year ago and has struggled to make his mark in East London.

As we covered extensively at the time, the selling club received only €8 million of the transfer fee, but the cost to the Hammers was considerably higher. It had been hoped that Pablo would be able to hit some goalscoring form in the Championship, but he has scored only twice in all competitions this campaign and has not featured in Scott Parker’s matchday squads.

His omission has been noted back in Portugal, with loan approaches made for the player. However, it is the valuation which has really taken the club aback.

Speaking to a transfer insider yesterday, Claret & Hugh were told: “There’s been practically no interest in Pablo. A couple of loan offers, one of which had an option to buy for €3m.”

Pablo price drop: West Ham have been left stunned by the market valuation of Pablo

That’s right, the highest offer West Ham have received for the 22-year-old includes a purchase option of just €3 million, suggesting his value has dropped by a whopping €17 million or more in under a year.

Of course, poor old Pablo was never worth that much to begin with. Gil Vicente paid his former Portuguese club Famalicão just €240,000 to sign the striker permanently six months before he was sold to the Hammers.

With West Ham looking to have something of a striker clearout in January, the scale of the potential losses from the big-money transfers of both Pablo and Taty Castellanos is beginning to be felt by the bean counters at Hammers HQ.

#2020. After moving from the Foxes exciting midfield prospect Christian Boothe signs Newcastle United professional contract

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

In late August, Christian Boothe was persuaded to move from Leicester City to Newcastle United.

The exciting teenage midfielder swapping the Foxes for the Magpies.

Now it has been revealed he has signed his first professional contract with Newcastle United on the day of his 17th birthday).

(ED: Players generally cannot sign a professional contract until their 17th birthday. Under The FA’s Rule C11, players must be 18 or over to enter a playing contract unless they are 17 and not in full-time education.)

A club statement on 28 August 2026 revealed that the young Leicester City starlet was one of three that Newcastle Unuted had persuaded to swap clubs as NUFC look to recruit the best young talent possible for the future: ‘Newcastle United can announce that promising youngsters Kyran Thompson, Christian Boothe and Kyle Healy-Matthews have joined the club’s Academy.  Thompson joins the club from Arsenal, with Boothe and Healy-Matthews arriving from Leicester City and West Ham United respectively.’

Having signed his Newcastle United pro contract, a now 17-year-old Christian Boothe reacting: “It is a surreal moment for me and my family, I’m so grateful to sign it with such a big club like Newcastle. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for me. I wanted to sign because there were better opportunities for different pathways into the first-team. I’m loving my time here. The name, Newcastle United, speaks for itself. Who wouldn’t want to join Newcastle? It’s a lovely club with so many good footballers that have played here. I’m also so lucky that I knew a few of the boys before I joined; Jayden (Kouossu), Muawiya (Ghanem) and Kyle (Healy-Matthews) as well because my brother played at West Ham. To have those friendships already definitely helped me to settle in.”

The exciting teenage midfield talent looking to take inspiration from Lewis Miley and Elliot Anderson: “You’ve seen the likes of Lewis and Elliot play for Newcastle’s first-team after coming through the Academy. I try to study their game and learn what I do differently to them and vice-versa, to try and follow in their footsteps. I’m really enjoying it at Newcastle so far and I think I’ve been performing well for the Under-18s. This season, I want to try and break into the Under-21s squad as well as train with the first-team. If I do get my shot with the first-team, it’s about making sure I express myself.”

Academy Director Steve Harper (pictured at the top of this article): “Christian has settled into life at Newcastle United really well since arriving last summer and we’re delighted to see him sign his first professional contract with the club. Joining a new environment always brings challenges, but he has adapted quickly, embraced the standards we expect and shown a strong commitment to developing his game. He’s worked hard to build relationships with his teammates and coaches, and that positive attitude has helped him make a strong start to his time here. This contract is recognition of the progress Christian has made so far, and we’re looking forward to continuing to support him as he develops and works towards achieving his potential.”

#2019. Behind the Goalkeeping Crisis Rocking West Ham

While Mads Hermansen’s recent performances have come under scrutiny and Finlay Herrick has found the transition challenging, culminating in his role in Portsmouth’s winning goal on Tuesday night, I still believe Herrick has the attributes to succeed. His potential is clear, but it requires time, guidance and development.

Meanwhile, supporters continue to ask why Alphonse Areola has not been available for first-team selection.

Let’s start with the facts. Alphonse Areola is no messiah. Last season, the French goalkeeper conceded 37 goals in 20 Premier League appearances, made 77 saves and failed to keep a single clean sheet. At the start of this season, Areola was informed that he was no longer Nuno’s first-choice goalkeeper. Despite having just one year remaining on his contract and reportedly taking a 50 per cent reduction in salary, now believed to be around £60,000 per week, no offers materialised. That still makes him one of the highest-paid goalkeepers in the Championship.

This season, he has been named on the bench nine times in 17 matches. However, questions remain over his fitness. Earlier in the campaign, he was sidelined with an unspecified injury despite being photographed attending a tennis tournament. He then reportedly suffered another setback during the warm-up ahead of the Blackburn Rovers match on 7 November, although the club has yet to officially disclose the nature of the injury.

Scott Parker has offered little clarity, saying only that “the club was struggling a bit with Alphonse” and describing his availability as “touch and go”. Inevitably, conspiracy theories have emerged, with some suggesting the goalkeeper has chosen not to make himself available for selection. However, there is no evidence to substantiate that suggestion, and he attended the Preston game with his family and watched from the stands.

The most likely explanation, as Martin previously outlined, is simply fitness, or a lack of it. For a club with only two recognised senior goalkeepers and one established academy option, the current situation is far from ideal.

While the team’s defensive issues cannot be blamed solely on the goalkeeping department, the number of goals conceded this season has undoubtedly affected results. It is an issue that requires an urgent resolution and one Parker will be acutely aware of.

Another area worth examining is the goalkeeping coaching set-up. Since Xavi Valero’s departure in May 2025, the club has never truly found a settled replacement. Casper Ankergren arrived alongside Linus Kandolin, Rui Barbosa subsequently replaced them and Billy Lepine later stepped into the role. In the space of just 18 months, the club has had four different goalkeeping coaches.

Continuity matters, particularly in such a specialised position, and that level of turnover is far from ideal.

For me, the club already has a ready-made solution in Łukasz Fabiański. His experience, leadership and understanding of the position make him more than qualified to take on such a responsibility.

Whatever the answer, Parker needs to resolve the situation quickly. The clock is ticking.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

I still don’t understand why Areola is unfit. He appears to have done nothing to get injured and I was physio for a major rugby union team for many years. My God, there is a difference between pro rugby players and footballers. If you look at a footballer the wrong way, send for the air-ambulance. Too much money in football.

With West Ham’s strikers continuing to struggle, Souček must start and, if he does, he has as good a chance of scoring as anyone on that football pitch.

#2016. West Ham’s January Transfer Plans Face Argentine Complication

West Ham United could be forced to wait until the summer if they are to sign River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán, according to the latest reports from Argentina. The Hammers have been linked with the highly rated goalkeeper for several weeks, but there appears to be a potential complication regarding the timing of any transfer.

Argentine journalist Juan Cortese has reported that River Plate could agree to sell Beltrán on the condition that he remains with the club until June. As reported this morning by The72, Aston Villa and Fiorentina are also showing interest in the goalkeeper.

West Ham’s interest in Beltrán comes as little surprise given Scott Parker’s ongoing goalkeeping problems. However, there is no suggestion that the Hammers have submitted an offer, and Cortese reports that West Ham are in no rush.

Personally, if West Ham have to wait until the summer for a goalkeeper, I see little point. By that time, dreams of a return to the Premier League will likely be over because I don’t believe there’s any chance of promotion with our current goalkeeping line-up.

The two immediate improvements Nils Koppen can make to the team in January are at goalkeeper and striker. With the Hammers already looking to offload Taty Castellanos, it’ll be interesting to see what business the club can get done.

Get it right and it’s not beyond the realms of possibility that West Ham can become a force in the division. But wait until June and we could find ourselves buying a goalkeeper for League One.

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It is Brighton v Newcastle United up next.

Fabian Hurzeler and his Seagulls taking on Matthias Jaissle’s Magpies.

Brighton v Newcastle United has never featured a Premier League away win for United.

In more than 35 years we have seen only one win for Newcastle at Brighton, a 2-1 Championship victory in the 2016-17 season, featuring that astonishing Mo Diame wonder goal!

Since the 1991-92 season there have only been 12 of these Brighton v Newcastle United matches but it is still not a place high on the expectation list for NUFC fans.

Brighton are second top in the Premier League of course and whilst Newcastle United got that excellent 2-2 draw with Arsenal, Fabian Hurzeler and his team smashed them 3-0 at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton have a Premier League record this season of Played 11 Won 7 Drawn 1 Lost 3.

In all competitions, Brighton’s record is Played 19 Won 12 Drawn 3 Lost 4.

However, the very daunting stats only appear ahead of this Brighton v Newcastle United match when you look at how the Seagulls have got on home and away.

In their 11 away matches in all competitions, Brighton have won 5, drawn 2 and lost 4, scoring 17 goals and conceding 13.

In their 8 home matches (all competitions), Brighton have won 7, drawn 1 and lost none, scoring 27 goals and conceding only 1!!

In over three months, the 1-1 Premier League draw against Leeds on 5 September 2026 is the only time this season that Brighton at home have conceded a goal, failed to win and not managed to score at least two goals on home turf.

The challenge is on for Newcastle United.

#2014. Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapses during post-match interview as journalist tries to break his fall after he 'felt dizzy' at the end of the first half of Boca Juniors' cup glory

Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026

Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors

The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf

'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'

Fortunately, Paredes was revived quickly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in New York at the World Cup final in July.

Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'

Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades)

'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'

Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'

#2013. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#2011. Parker’s West Ham Snowball Is Already Gathering Pace

Scott Parker was in a particularly festive mood during yesterday’s pre-match press conference ahead of West Ham’s clash with Stoke City on Saturday. The Hammers gaffer trotted out a rather obscure festive analogy about snowballs getting bigger, which is all very well and good.

But if he’s not careful, that little ball of ice could start hurtling down a mountainside and become an avalanche. West Ham are now six games without a victory, and Parker is still awaiting his first win as head coach.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker said: “You have to make sure that little snowball doesn’t become a massive one, and that’s certainly something that’s on my mind.”

One of the things I most liked about Parker’s first couple of interviews was that he didn’t revert to football clichés, and his snowball comparison certainly wasn’t one. But it came amid the usual talk of having to do better and his assertion that we’ll be judged in May.

Probably what concerned me most was that he feels performances have been good. I do believe the Hammers boss is relying heavily on data, and that is something that could be misleading. As the old adage goes, there are lies, damned lies and statistics.

Make no mistake about it, West Ham’s attacking statistics were heavily boosted by a flurry of activity, largely initiated by Tomáš Souček, between the 85th and 90th minutes. By and large, throughout the game at Fratton Park, his team were easily contained.

There are two things Parker must prioritise against Stoke, and it’s going to be a tricky thing to balance because not only must West Ham score first, but they must also ensure that Stoke don’t do the same.

Whoever Parker picks between the sticks will need protecting

Therefore, Parker is going to be caught between a rock and a hard place, wanting to protect whichever nervous goalkeeper is between the sticks whilst trying to ensure West Ham are not left chasing the game from a deficit.

I think it may well mean we’re in for a cagey affair because, whilst the game remains at nil-nil, the worst hasn’t happened. I’m not sure how good that will be for a nervous London Stadium crowd.

Somehow, the Irons boss must get his message across to players who look very short on motivation, which is a concern bearing in mind the manager has only been in the Hammers hot seat for five minutes.

Whether that rousing rallying cry comes in the form of snowballs, chimneys or Santa’s sleigh matters not. Because if Parker doesn’t get a massive improvement from the next few games, he may well find that snowball makes for a very unjolly Christmas.

#2010. “West Ham Captaincy” The Jarrod Bowen Question Nobody Seems To Be Asking

West Ham United captain Jarrod Bowen has dismissed suggestions that the Hammers’ struggles to adapt to Championship football can be used as an excuse for their poor performances. Speaking to talkSPORT last night, Bowen acknowledged that the players simply haven’t been good enough.

The West Ham skipper remains confident that the club can secure promotion back to the Premier League, despite the Hammers having slipped to 13th in the Championship. With second-placed Stoke City visiting the London Stadium on Saturday, Scott Parker is still searching for his first victory as head coach.

When asked about the difficulties of adapting to the Championship, Bowen said: “We can’t lean on that too much, we just have to face up to the facts that we haven’t been good enough.” The Hammers captain also touched upon his playing position during the interview, which was arguably one of the more interesting aspects of the discussion.

I’m pleased that Jarrod Bowen said West Ham haven’t been good enough, but having listened to the talkSPORT interview, I couldn’t help but think that he was trotting out what was expected of him. Understandably, the line of questioning was rather generic.

Personally, I’d have liked to know why Bowen has been stuck out on the wing and been so ineffective for much of the last three games. The Hammers skipper alluded to the fact that he’d not discussed his position with Parker, which I find astounding considering the influence Bowen had in a free role against Cardiff City.

As for the West Ham captaincy, well, the less said about that the better. As Portsmouth went 1-0 up on Tuesday night, a distraught Fin Herrick lay on the ground beating his fist in frustration. He’s a rookie keeper who, in my opinion, had made another mistake and needed guidance.

What did Bowen do? Despite standing next to Herrick, Bowen turned on his heels, dropped his head and walked away, leaving the academy prospect to pick himself up and deal with it. Unacceptable.

Ideally, I’d have preferred a tougher line of questioning, drilling down into the specifics of exactly what is going on with West Ham’s best player. Instead, we got clichéd responses and a pledge that we’ll be involved in the promotion shake-up in May.

#2009. “Forget About It” Agent Dismisses West Ham Transfer Link

West Ham United are not pursuing a transfer for River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán, according to a well-known football agent speaking to Claret & Hugh this afternoon. The Argentine has been linked with a move to the London Stadium for several weeks as the Hammers look to resolve their goalkeeping problems.

Earlier today, Claret & Hugh reported that River Plate could be reluctant to part with Beltrán until the summer. However, it would appear that West Ham’s January recruitment plans lie elsewhere.

When we put the latest transfer reports to a well-known football agent this afternoon, the response was emphatic: “You can forget about Beltrán going to West Ham. They’re looking for a keeper, I’ve seen four or five mentioned and he wasn’t on the list.”

Beltran will not be heading to West Ham in January

Perhaps the most encouraging aspect of our conversation this afternoon is that the Hammers are looking at several goalkeepers ahead of the January transfer window.

With Alphonse Areola struggling with fitness and Scott Parker alternating between Mads Hermansen and Fin Herrick, it’s a position that needs addressing sooner rather than later.

Whilst our source didn’t identify the other goalkeepers being considered, it would appear that Beltrán is not currently among them.

#2008. OLIVER HOLT: Man United ARE in a relegation battle - anybody who denies it is deluding themselves - and Mauricio Pochettino is already showing signs of cracking under pressure

Published: 07:54 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:31 EST, 23 November 2026

Early on in On the Road, somewhere between Chicago and Denver, Jack Kerouac described the journey his main character was taking and some of the trepidation that came with each new horizon. ‘I was halfway across America,’ he wrote, ‘at the dividing line between the East of my youth and the West of my future.’

Late on Sunday afternoon, as winter’s grey light turned to darkness on Merseyside and a bitter wind blew in off the Irish Sea, Manchester United’s new boss, Mauricio Pochettino, freshly arrived from Cincinnati, Ohio, arms folded grimly and tightly across his chest, stood on the touchline at Anfield and realised the full extent of what he had just got himself into.

Sure, the United job was too big to turn down. However far the club has fallen, it still has that lure. It still has the name, even if the name is now just one of those building facades on a film set.

There is the name and then there is the nothingness that is concealed beyond the name. There is the mismanaged, mistreated void that United has become.

And now United need to find out which version of Pochettino they have purchased. Because he is at a dividing line, too. Do they have the Pochettino who blazed a trail across the football landscape with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs, although he did not win trophies at any of those destinations?

Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation gradually became becalmed at Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA national team? They better hope they can restart something in him because this is the biggest and the hardest job Pochettino has ever had and it will take a Herculean effort just to survive.

Do Man United have the Mauricio Pochettino who blazed a trail with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs? Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation has fluctuated since?

That is what this season is about now for these fallen, ruined giants. It is about survival. Nothing more. If Pochettino did not realise it before, he will have realised it during that calamitous 4-0 defeat at Anfield: United are in a relegation battle and anyone who denies that is deluding themselves.

That is just pride talking. The remnants of what pride remains at United, anyway.

Maybe it hasn’t quite seemed real until now. Just like the prospect of Leicester City winning the Premier League didn’t start to feel real until around Christmas of 2015-16. United going down would be up there with Leicester winning the title in terms of seismic events in the modern English game. It’s time to start taking relegation seriously.

If you take the blinkers off for just a second, if you banish the muscle memory that tells you United are too successful and too rich to get sucked down into the Championship, then you have to accept that all the ingredients are there for United to get relegated. Take that name away and what’s left?

What’s left is a team that last won a Premier League game on August 30. What’s left is a team that has won one game all season. What’s left is a team that has conceded 34 goals across all competitions, more than any other team in Europe's top five leagues. What’s left is a team that has eight points from its first 11 league games.

Just for context, the Spurs side that spent most of last season haunted by the prospect of relegation, had 18 points at this stage of that campaign. If you still think the rabble currently representing the club are too good to go down, I think you are deluding yourself.

Yes, United played more than 80 minutes of the game against Liverpool with 10 men and, yes, the decision to send off Leny Yoro for his challenge on Alexander Isak was harsh. But the dismissal was also a fig-leaf for Pochettino and United. It was convenient. It was a disguise for what lay beneath.

United also brought it on themselves. Pochettino made one big selection decision before the game when he picked Matthijs de Ligt ahead of Harry Maguire. It was what former bosses in the English game might have described as a ‘big rick’. It was a terrible misjudgment.

Maybe the sending off of Leny Yoro was harsh. But United brought it on themselves

Matthijs de Ligt (right) was bullied by Alexander Isak at Anfield. Pochettino's decision to play the Dutchman was a terrible misjudgment

De Ligt’s first action was to watch a long ball from Ronald Araujo sail over his head, gazing at it with a mix of horror and wonder, as you might if you were watching the trajectory of an alien spaceship. Yoro was not quick enough to read De Ligt’s discomfort and so the horror ensued.

It was Pochettino’s first game and it is impossible to judge him yet but it is possible to say this was a bad start.

There were even a couple of worrying signs in his post-match press conference when the bonhomie and the relaxed demeanour that are among his great strengths deserted him.

When he was asked about United being in the relegation zone, he snapped that it was a ‘cheap’ question because he had only just arrived at the club. He said he saw fight in his players, which few others had seen. He blamed everything on the sending off of Yoro, even though it was his selection of De Ligt that had led to it.

A few alarm bells started to ring. Only faintly and only in the distance but they were ringing nonetheless. Pochettino has had big jobs before but he has never had a job as big as Manchester United where the scrutiny and the expectation and the judgment is relentless and unforgiving.

Pochettino has dealt with Daniel Levy at Spurs, which may not have been an easy relationship, but he has never dealt with a clown-show like the one that Jim Ratcliffe has put in place at Old Trafford.

United is rotten. Everyone can see that. Off the pitch, the club is at war with its own fans. The club gives every impression of trying to move on its most loyal supporters so that it can replace them with tourists and day-trippers who will spend more on tickets and in the club superstore and at the food stands.

‘The way you treat us is a disgrace,’ that banner in the Stretford End said a few weeks ago, and that is how the fans feel. They are more loyal than United deserve but their patience with their owners ran out a long time ago. Pochettino has a disaffected fanbase to deal with as well.

United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight. It feels as if it is getting weaker and weaker and weaker. And when Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next week, they will smell blood. Every club that comes to Old Trafford now smells blood.

Harry Maguire looks dejected at full-time on Sunday. United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight

Still think they’re too good to go down? Who are they better than in this league? Hull City? United don’t have the spirit of Hull City. They don’t have the togetherness. They don’t have the pride.

Hull got battered by Brighton on Sunday afternoon and still won 2-0. United could never have done that. United have already lost to Hull and Brighton this season, too.

So, yes, United are in a relegation fight. They’re one off the bottom of the league in the last week of November. Of course, they’re in a relegation fight. It’s on their new boss to get them out of it.

If Pochettino is on the wrong side of the dividing line of his career, if the best part of his journey is behind him, United are in big, big trouble.

#2007. West Ham Need A Different Approach As £12m Target Breaks Silence

FC Midtjylland winger Mikel Gogorza has confirmed that West Ham United submitted a concrete transfer offer for him during the summer window. The 20-year-old has also revealed that playing in England remains his dream, despite rejecting the opportunity to join the Hammers.

Speaking to Danish publication Bold following Midtjylland’s 2-0 Conference League victory over Pafos last night, Gogorza explained that the offer arrived whilst he was recovering from a groin injury. According to an English translation of the interview published by Sport Witness, West Ham’s bid was worth approximately £12 million.

Gogorza revealed that both he and his club felt it was important for him to spend another season in Denmark following his injury. With the January transfer window approaching and Scott Parker’s team struggling for attacking inspiration, it’ll be interesting to see whether the Hammers revisit any of their summer transfer targets.

I’d certainly be hoping that West Ham wouldn’t be revisiting their interest in Gogorza, primarily because I don’t believe him to be an upgrade on what we have. He certainly doesn’t appear to be worth a £18 million gamble which is the number currently being quoted.

Look, the jury is still out on Edvin Austbø, who appears to be a promising player. But I’m firmly of the opinion that West Ham do need another winger, ideally one who’s versatile enough to play on both sides.

It would be my preference to have somebody with experience of English football, and I’m intrigued to find out where Nils Koppen has been focusing his interest.

It’s worth remembering that last summer, as Claret & Hugh exclusively revealed at the time, the Hammers hierarchy hired Ben Chorley to assist with identifying Championship-based players.

#2006. Liverpool ‘showing concrete interest’ in Bundesliga wonderkid Jurgen Klopp likes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a new contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be said, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”

The big issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

#2005. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”
